headline: How a Rehab Clinic Rebuilt Its Google Ads Into a Measured Phone-Lead Engine
summary_line: PPC Guru took a rehabilitation clinic off a minimal-budget Smart Campaign — one whose recorded 'conversions' were mostly Google Maps directions and button taps — and rebuilt it into two focused Search campaigns with genuine call and JaneApp booking tracking. The result is a dependable, measurable stream of around 22 real phone-call leads a month in the most recent quarter (Apr–Jun 2026), at roughly $63 per lead.
client_context: The client is a rehabilitation clinic in Ontario, Canada offering physiotherapy and massage therapy, with patient scheduling handled through the JaneApp booking and practice-management system. Like most local clinics, its growth depends on a steady flow of new-patient enquiries — mainly phone calls from people searching for treatment nearby. Google Ads is the clinic's primary channel for reaching those high-intent searchers, which makes reliable measurement of calls and bookings central to the account's success.
background: For several years the account ran as a low-budget Google Smart Campaign, spending only around $300 a month. It logged plenty of 'conversions', but on inspection most were Google local actions — map-direction requests and click-to-call taps on the Business Profile — rather than separately tracked phone-call leads or bookings. The clinic had little real visibility into how many genuine enquiries the spend produced. In late 2022 the account was handed to PPC Guru for a full rebuild focused on measurement and controllable Search campaigns.
analysis: Before scaling anything, PPC Guru audited the account's long history, conversion tracking and campaign structure. The review showed genuine local demand but a measurement gap: the Smart Campaign optimized toward whatever was easiest to trigger — directions and profile taps — instead of real calls and bookings. The plan put honest tracking first, moved the account onto dedicated Search campaigns, and only then scaled budget against measured phone-call leads.
analysis_points: Rebuild conversion tracking to capture genuine phone calls (from ads and the website) and JaneApp bookings, and separate them from Google local actions.
Move off the Smart Campaign onto dedicated Search campaigns for physiotherapy and massage therapy, for full control of keywords and budget.
Use Maximize Conversions bidding once trustworthy call data was flowing.
Scale budget deliberately against measured phone-call leads rather than vanity local actions.

timeline.what: Pre-rebuild baseline — a minimal-budget Smart Campaign (~$300/mo) whose recorded conversions were mostly Google local actions, not separately tracked calls.
PPC Guru rebuild — genuine call tracking wired up (first tracked phone-call leads from Sep 2022) and the account moved toward dedicated Search campaigns.
First full year of measured leads; the new Search structure and budget were established at roughly $1,500–2,000 a month.
The account settled into a steady ~17–22 genuine phone-call leads a month with call and JaneApp booking tracking in place.
About 22 genuine phone-call leads a month at roughly $63 per lead, from two focused Search campaigns.

challenge: The account had years of history and a healthy-looking conversion count, but the numbers were misleading. Running as a low-budget Smart Campaign, it recorded mostly Google Maps directions and click-to-call taps — local actions, not measurable enquiries. There was no reliable line of sight from ad spend to a genuine phone call or a booked appointment, which made it impossible to know what was actually working or to scale with confidence.

changes.change: Moved off Smart Campaign to Search
changes.why: Two dedicated Search campaigns (physiotherapy and massage therapy) gave full control over keywords, budget and negatives instead of an automated black box.
Separated real phone-call leads (from ads and the website) from Google local actions so reporting reflected actual enquiries.
Wired completed bookings from JaneApp back into the account so optimisation could aim at patients, not button taps.
Once genuine call signals were trustworthy, automated bidding could chase real enquiries efficiently.
Spend was increased from ~$300/mo toward ~$1,400/mo only after measured phone leads confirmed the channel worked.
Continuous negative-keyword work kept traffic relevant to treatment-intent searches as volume grew.

benchmark: * In the pre-rebuild era the account ran as a low-budget Smart Campaign, and genuine phone-call leads were not tracked separately from Google local actions (map directions and click-to-call taps). The comparison therefore contrasts the earlier setup with today's measured program rather than two identical lead counts. Since genuine tracking began, quarterly phone-call leads have grown from about 13 a month in the first tracked quarter to about 22 a month in Q2 2026.

early_stage.title: The First Measured Quarter
early_stage.intro: Once genuine call tracking was in place, the account began recording real phone-call leads for the first time. The first full tracked quarter (Q4 2022) produced about 39 genuine calls — roughly 13 a month — a modest but honest starting point that the rebuilt Search structure grew from.

gradual: Rather than spiking once and fading, the account matured into a steady lead engine. Through 2024 it averaged about 17 genuine phone-call leads a month, climbing to roughly 20–22 a month across 2025 and into 2026 as targeting and negatives tightened. The monthly trend below shows the natural month-to-month variation of a real clinic account — including a quieter May 2026 when spend was reduced — around a consistent, measurable baseline of genuine calls.

spotlight.title: Why the JaneApp Booking Integration Matters
spotlight.body: JaneApp is the clinic's booking and practice-management system. Feeding genuine phone calls and completed bookings back into Google Ads — instead of counting Maps directions and profile taps — is what turned a vanity conversion count into an honest one. It lets automated bidding chase real patient enquiries, and it gives the clinic a true picture of which searches produce booked treatment. Without that closed loop, Google optimises toward whatever is cheapest to trigger, which is exactly how the account behaved before the rebuild.

lessons: A high conversion count means nothing if most of it is Maps directions and profile taps — track genuine calls and bookings.
Smart Campaigns trade control for convenience; a dedicated Search campaign lets you steer budget toward treatment-intent searches.
Get honest measurement in place before scaling budget, not after.
Feed real bookings back into the account so bidding optimises toward patients, not button clicks.
Expect natural month-to-month variation; judge the account on its steady baseline, not any single month.
why_it_worked: Honest call and booking tracking replaced a conversion count inflated by Google local actions.
Dedicated Search campaigns gave full control over keywords, budget and negatives.
Budget was scaled only after measured phone leads proved the channel worked.
Ongoing search-term hygiene kept traffic focused on genuine treatment-intent queries.
outcome: Today the clinic runs on a measured, controllable Search program instead of an automated Smart Campaign. In the most recent complete quarter (April–June 2026) it generated about 22 genuine phone-call leads a month at roughly $63 per lead, with call and JaneApp booking tracking giving a true view of demand — up from a pre-rebuild setup that recorded mostly Maps directions and profile taps rather than real enquiries. Because every dollar of spend is now tied to genuine calls and bookings, the clinic can scale with confidence rather than guesswork.
cta: PPC Guru helps Canadian clinics turn search traffic into genuine phone-call and booking enquiries with conversion-focused Google Ads and transparent reporting.
methodology: All figures are pulled directly from the client's Google Ads account and shown on a monthly basis. 'Leads' are genuine phone-call conversions (calls from ads and the website); Google local actions — map directions, click-to-call taps, website visits — are excluded so counts reflect real enquiries. 'Now' is the most recent complete quarter (April–June 2026). Before the late-2022 rebuild, genuine phone-call leads were not separately tracked, so the earlier period is described rather than counted.
lead_quality: Genuine leads here are direct phone calls — the highest-intent enquiry type for a rehabilitation clinic — tracked from both ads and the website, with completed JaneApp bookings measured alongside.
